our_interpretation: In context, the claim concerns contemporary image generators' ability to satisfy simple functional design instructions.

The plain reading is recurring failure to apply a requirement such as one-handed operation when generating designs. It does not require every output to fail: the supplied footnote expressly allows successful outputs.
Understanding is assessed through observable compliance with the requested function, without claiming that an image test establishes a system's internal mental state.
No reporting period is specified. I use February 2024 through the publication date, the latest partial month describing the ongoing state, rather than later systems' capabilities.
Marcus specifies neither a failure-rate threshold nor a representative set of systems. Isolated selected examples cannot establish typical performance across systems.
criteria.support_condition: Documented, repeated tests of contemporary image generators show recurring failures to meet plainly stated functional requirements, including one-handed controller operation, across ordinary prompt variants and unselected outputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable tests show that contemporary image generators reliably satisfy these functional requirements with ordinary instructions. An isolated success following detailed design instructions would not suffice.
